criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: The deck holds the dark staged register throughout. Slide 1 is the best frame: a white tractor on a diamond-tread scale deck, yellow kerb rails converging, a lit green signal, true blacks and a bright flood edge. It reads at 432 px. Slides 5, 6 and 7 are real TXBENCH reliefs. render_report gives height_range 70.5, 30.2 and 114, with 5, 5 and 6 materials and visible casts, and their encodings read at feed size: six week segments, a thin billet against the long loss bar, a white inlay against primer studs. Several frames fall short of 'strong overall'. Slide 9, the close, is the measured payoff, and its stall encoding does not read. The primer stalls fade into the dark with no visible 200 or 1,000 boundary. The three labels float over orange lines that mark nothing a reader can identify, and '20+ built' sits over primer stalls rather than white ones. Slide 4's twenty tractors fill a band about 30 percent of the frame high, with roughly 380 px of empty asphalt under the near rank, and at thumb size they read as a toy lot. On slide 3 the gate cabinet is a rounded box with a sphere lamp, a primitive model, and the right half is empty mid-dark. Slide 8 is lit gold and sepia, out of key with the cold flood of slides 1 to 4. Its beacon reads as a pale yellow dome rather than a lit amber lamp, and no shoulder reads under the wheels to say 'stopped'. On slide 2 the 'scale configuration' leader ends on the scale house wall rather than the third ring, and that label is set at 23 px, under the 24 px floor (machine_qa warn).

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: This is clearly one deck: one night world under one cold flood, one steel, concrete and asphalt vocabulary, and a rust primer accent that means only 'what the letter says will happen'. Primer sits on 3, 5, 6, 7 and 9, and the contact sheet confirms it. The scale motif evolves from scale deck (1, 2) to rule (5) to datum (6) to stall paint (9). The storyboard declares the cut at frame 5, and the filmstrip shows it as the turn into reliefs. Slide 8 sits outside the deck: its warm gold key and bright mid-tone truck are the one frame whose light differs from the rest. Slide 9's yard does return slide 4's yard, as planned.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every slide numeral traces to the claims. 20+ (c1), 500,000 and 100% (c2), 20 a week (c11), $3M, $257M and about $9M (c13, c14, c12), 500, 2027 and 2028 (c3, c4), 200 and 1,000 (c15, c16), five-year (c20), and three steps is computed (scale_steps). All sources are primary: the SEC EDGAR letter and Aurora's IR release. The copy attributes company figures as self-report ('by Aurora's own count', 'the letter says'). Charger's Dallas to Laredo is kept as a plan under a non-binding MOU, and the slide 7 dek states that routes are drawn straight. Two phrasings run looser than the record. The cover says 'if the scale is open' where c9 says 'a station is open', which is defensible trucker usage. Slide 9's dek asserts 'Each primer stall is one expected truck', an encoding a reader can't verify in the frame, because the field fades into the dark before any count is visible.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan learns what happened and who said it: Aurora, in its October 28th SEC letter, says its trucks now handle weigh stations and will drive into customer sites in November. The deck is honest about the cost side, with the six week slip and $3M of revenue against a $257M loss. It also names Texas places: Dallas to Houston, Charger's Dallas to Laredo plan and New Braunfels/AUMOVIO. Texas first appears on slide 7 of 9, though. The cover and kickers never place the weigh station in Texas, and the web edition concedes the letter names no Texas station or site. The only next step offered is reading the filing on EDGAR. The docket's public_access is 'contact_only', so a reader is left with nothing to act on and no Texas body or deadline. The stake for a driver on I-45 is stated generally.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover hook is concrete and earns a swipe. Slide 2 pays off at once by naming the three calls on one station. The deck turns at slide 5 ('About six weeks behind its own plan'), where understanding changes from capability to the company's own numbers. Slide 8, the FMCSA beacon exemption, is a capability or regulatory frame stranded between the Texas map and the close. It could move up beside 2 and 3 without loss. The close's numbers land in type, but its image doesn't deliver the 20 to 1,000 distance.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Plainspoken and dry, with real road vernacular ('scale lane', 'scale house'). The caption opener, 'Aurora told its shareholders about weigh stations.', is good, and so is its closing question, 'Has a Texas scale house weighed a driverless Aurora truck yet?'. It is neither boosterish nor doom. A few lines read as machine footnotes rather than a writer: slide 7's 'Routes drawn straight between places. New Braunfels is marked at Comal County's center.' and slide 9's 'Each primer stall is one expected truck. The filing is on the SEC's EDGAR site, dated October 28th.' No colons, semicolons, em dashes or banned words seen.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The concept, a weigh station traversal turned into a scale motif, is fresh, and the scene and relief mix differs from no. 66, no. 65, no. 64 and no. 63. Familiar moves remain. The floodlit night apron under a cold flood repeats no. 47 and no. 59. A vehicle at night opened no. 66 the day before. This is also the third AV deck in 18 days, after Waymo (no. 52) and Tesla (no. 59). It is not a topic repeat: tx-2026-0239 is new and no Aurora deck appears in the 30 day window.

named_defects: Slide 9: the stall encoding the dek announces is not readable. No 200 or 1,000 boundary is visible, the labels float over unexplained orange lines, and '20+ built' sits on primer stalls rather than the white ones.
Slide 4: the subject is a thin band of toy-scale tractors with about 380 px of empty asphalt below the near rank.
Slide 3: the gate cabinet is a primitive rounded box with a sphere lamp. The primer stop bar is a flat strip barely in the light, and the right half of the frame is empty.
Slide 8: a warm gold key breaks the deck's cold flood. The beacon reads as a pale yellow dome, and no shoulder is visible.
Slide 2: the 'scale configuration' leader ends on the scale house wall rather than the third ring, and the label is 23 px, under the 24 px mobile floor.
Reader: Texas is not placed until slide 7, and the deck offers no Texas body, deadline or way in beyond reading the filing.
Sequence: slide 8 is out of order between the map and the close.
Voice: the slide 7 and slide 9 deks end in mechanical disclaimer sentences.
one_sentence_fix: Rebuild slide 9 so its own encoding reads at feed size, the 20 white stalls, a lit block of 200 primer stalls with a scribed edge, and the 1,000 field running into the dark as three visibly different areas, each label leadered to the boundary it names.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The close's measured scale doesn't read. The primer stalls fade into the dark with no visible 200 or 1,000 boundary, and '20+ built' sits over primer rather than white stalls.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Raise the mast camera toward plan view at fov 30, light a bounded block of 200 primer stalls beside the 20 white ones, scribe a primer edge at the 200 boundary, end each label's leader on its edge, and move '20+ built' onto the white stalls.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Twenty tractors in a band about 30 percent of the frame high, with roughly 380 px of empty asphalt under the near rank.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Drop the eye to about 4 m and dolly in about 25 percent so the near casts and stall stripes fill the bottom third while the far rank still holds ten countable cabs.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The gate cabinet is a rounded box with a sphere lamp. The primer stop bar is outside the headlamp pool, and the right half is empty mid-dark.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Model the cabinet with panel seams, a hinge hub, a hooded amber lamp housing and a card reader post, and put the primer stop bar inside the headlamp pool with a contact shadow.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A gold, sepia key breaks the deck's cold flood. The beacon dome is pale yellow, and no shoulder reads.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Re-key to the deck's cold flood so the cab is steel-white, make the beacon dome emissive amber as the one warm light, and lower the camera to show the shoulder edge line under the front wheel.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The 'scale configuration' leader ends on the scale house wall, not on the third ring. The label is 23 px.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: End that leader within 24 px of the third ring and set the label at 26 px on a single line.
